Hi Elena — thanks for the clear asks. Quick summary up-front: Redwood acknowledges the likely high-risk classification for clinical decision support in the EU AI Act context and we provide both product controls and deployment options that materially reduce the regulatory exposure. Attached is a focused addendum and a mapping sheet to NIST AI RMF controls.

Short answers to your three bullets (details & artifacts attached):

1) EU AI Act / high-risk positioning: 
- Positioning: We treat clinical decision support as a high-risk application when used to influence clinical decisions. Our recommended approach is a combination of (a) Private deployment (VPC / on-prem) + Dedicated capacity to ensure data residency, (b) enforced human-in-the-loop gating for any recommended action, and (c) stronger explainability outputs (structured rationale + provenance token indices) to support documentation.
- Mitigations: model cards (per-version), mandatory canary rollout with guarded thresholds, audit logging of tokens and KV cache traces for the decision window, and KMS-backed request-level encryption for PHI.

2) NIST AI RMF mapping: 
- See tab 'NIST_Mapping' in the attached spreadsheet for identify/protect/detect/respond/recover entries. Examples: continuous model performance monitors -> Detect; automated rollback policies tied to metric breaches -> Respond; model provenance & immutable artifacts -> Protect/Identify.

3) Regression / evaluation plan: 
- Sampling: stratified sampling by patient cohort, clinical condition, and time-window; reserve a temporal holdout for drift detection.
- Acceptance criteria: specificity/sensitivity thresholds per cohort (we provide configurable defaults), plus falsenegative-rate ceilings for high-risk cohorts.
- Drift & labeling: automated drift detectors (KL divergence on embeddings + feature-shift detection), label drift flagged for human-in-loop relabel campaigns and retraining windows.
- Data retention: evaluation sets stored encrypted for 90 days by default (configurable), with policies to export masks/anonymize for audit.

Attachments included: a short addendum PDF, an xlsx NIST/EU mapping, and the regression-harness spec. 

We can host a 45m follow-up with your security team tomorrow (Nov 3, 10:00–11:00 ET). If that works for you I will add Marissa (product lead) and Neha (research/ops) to the calendar.

Regards,

Thanks — I reviewed the addendum and the regression-harness spec. Quick technical confirmations and a suggested tweak: 

1) Retention: 90 days is our default to balance auditability and storage costs; we offer configurable retention up to 365 days under an enterprise compliance add-on. For medical use cases we recommend at least 180 days if the customer needs longitudinal audits.

2) HIL thresholds: the proposed confidence threshold of 0.65 is a reasonable starting point. For Argentum's triage use case I recommend cohort-specific calibration: lower thresholds for well-represented cohorts, stricter thresholds (0.75+) for low-signal cohorts. We will include a calibration run in the regression harness to produce recommended thresholds per cohort.

3) Token-level provenance: feasible. We recommend storing provenance indices (offsets + hashed tokens) rather than raw text. That reduces storage and avoids storing PHI directly. We also suggest a rolling 30-day provenance index by default; longer windows available as a configurable option.

4) NIST mapping: I filled in the 'NIST_Mapping' tab with concrete controls (e.g., ID.AM-ModelInventory, PR.DS-EncryptionAtRest, DE-1:AutomatedAnomalyDetection, RS-2:AutomatedRollbackPolicy).

I'll attach a short snippet of the regression harness config that shows: sampling code (stratified temporal holdout), metrics collected (cohort-sensitivity, cohort-specific FNR, calibration error, embedding-KL drift), and the automated escalation flow.

Accepting the Nov 3 10:00 ET follow-up. Olga — please send the calendar invite. Elena — feel free to forward this to your audit folks; happy to go through any of the artifacts live.

-Neha
